Chinese stocks swung into gains as inflows into a basket of exchange-traded funds favored by the national team picked up pace.
The onshore benchmark CSI 300 Index gained as much as 1.1% in afternoon trading, erasing a drop of up to 1.9%. The advance trims the gauge’s decline from its June peak after it entered a bear market on Thursday.

Technology stocks trimmed their losses heading into the European session, offering global investors some respite after renewed pressure on the artificial intelligence trade drove demand for bonds. Crude oil extended its gains.

Singapore Exchange Ltd. Chief Executive Officer Loh Boon Chye is planning to step down after more than a decade at the helm, with a new leader yet to be named.
“We have a clear strategic direction, a very capable leadership team and the momentum to take SGX much further,” Loh said at the company’s annual meeting on Friday. “With this in mind, I recently shared with our chairman that we should begin planning ahead for an eventual transition in the CEO role.”

Save
Fallout from MSCI Inc.’s warning that it may remove Indonesia from its global equity indexes is spilling into the country’s corporate credit.
The extra yield that investors demand to hold the notes over regional peers has jumped 28 basis points to 67 basis points, the widest since 2020, after the MSCI move, Bloomberg indexes show. The blowout shows how the possible downgrade by the index provider is fueling deeper-seated concerns about governance in Southeast Asia’s largest economy.

Volvo AB said improving demand in North America and Europe helped deliver solid earnings during the third quarter with the truckmaker planning to gradually increase production.
Adjusted operating profit rose to 14.7 billion kronor ($1.32 billion) in the three months through September, the Swedish manufacturer said Friday. Total truck order intake increased by 26%.

Swiggy Ltd. shares fell to a record low after intense competition led to wider-than-expected loss at the Indian rapid-commerce contender, raising questions about its long-term earnings potential.
The stock tumbled 17% in Mumbai for its biggest intra-day slide on record. The shares have lost more than half their value since the company’s 2024 initial public offering, leaving it with a market value of $5.2 billion.
